sections.html:
In Catawba County one office does the listing, appraising, assessing and collecting for all real and personal property. Call (828) 465-8414 with general questions and (828) 465-8436 to book a tax relief appointment. Relief applications can be mailed to Assessor's Office, Attn: Tax Relief, Box 368, Newton, NC 28658-0368.

If you are selling, this is where you get a written statement of what a parcel owes, find out whether a relief claim or deferment is on file, and learn which fire district or town your address belongs to. Have the parcel number or your bill ready, and have staff list each open year separately so nothing slips past closing.

The office has earned the Certificate of Excellence in Assessment Administration from the International Association of Assessing Officers. Your own bill depends on the parcel's value, the county rate, and the fire district or town where the parcel sits.

sections.h2: County, town and fire district rates
sections.html:
The county rate is .3985 per $100 of assessed value, and every parcel also pays either a fire district tax or a municipal tax. The county tax page prints the full list. Main figures are below.

Fire districts run from .061 for Oxford to .13 for Claremont Rural. Others include Cooksville at .0785, Propst at .072, Mtn View at .0855, Maiden Rural at .0983, Sherrills Ford/Terrell at .099, Conover Rural and Long View Rural at .10, Bandys at .1050, Catawba Rural at .117, Newton Rural at .121, St Stephens at .124 and Hickory Rural at .125.

A parcel inside a town or city pays that municipality's rate. A parcel outside pays the fire district rate that covers it. Check your bill or ask the tax office which applies, then add it to the county rate for the combined figure.

Catawba County revalues every four years. Values now in use date from January 1, 2023. The following countywide revaluation is effective January 1, 2027. State law requires one only every eight years, so the county moves twice as fast. Staff are studying sales and market trends for the 2027 round.

New appeals open after the 2027 notices go out, in January 2027. The path starts with an informal review and moves up only if that fails:

  • Once value notices go out, ask the tax office how to start an informal review, using the form enclosed with the notice.
  • When that fails, the county board of equalization and review is next. Ask for a hearing in writing or in person before adjournment.
  • After the board, the state Property Tax Commission hears appeals made by written notice within 30 days of the mailed ruling.

Revaluation updates values, not rates. The rate is set in the annual budget ordinance, usually finalized in June. An appeal can lower your value but cannot change the rate.

Four programs are offered: the elderly or disabled homestead exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion, the circuit breaker deferment, and AV-10 applications for other exclusions. An owner may pick only one of the first three.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: for owners who were 65 or disabled on January 1, own the home, live in the county and report income under the printed limit. The reduction is the greater of $25,000 or half the appraised value. A 65-plus applicant skips the disability certificate, and approval carries forward until you move, sell, rent, change the deed or go over the income limit.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: up to $45,000 of a permanent residence's assessed value is removed, and income is not tested. The county wants discharge papers plus VA certification of permanent, total, service-connected disability, or proof of specially adapted housing benefits.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: the bill is limited to 4 or 5 percent of income for owners with five or more years of living in and owning the home. The deferred part is a lien, repayable with interest for the current year and three earlier ones once the property transfers.

June 1 is the yearly cutoff for all three, and the circuit breaker needs a new application every year. The AV-10 for religious, charitable, historic and similar exclusions is filed in January. The 2026 income limit is $38,800, with $58,200 as the 150 percent mark for the circuit breaker.

Sale proceeds clear whatever tax is open. Each year's lien attaches on the January 1 listing date, and the bill is due September 1. Every parcel pays county tax plus a fire or town levy, so a Hickory payoff will not match one for a house in a rural fire district.

No interest is charged through January 5. From January 6 interest is 2 percent through January, and three-fourths of a percent for each month after.

Circuit breaker owners get the surprise: transferring the property is a disqualifying event, so the deferred amounts become payable at the sale. Ask the tax office for a statement showing the current bill and any deferred balance.

Deed charges belong to the Register of Deeds, a separate office, and the seller pays the state excise tax there before recording. Get the written tax statement first and hand it to your closing attorney, who builds the payoff into the settlement statement. A cash sale has no lender payoff to line up, yet the tax balance is still paid at closing.

Before listing, read your latest value notice and compare the assessed value with recent sales nearby. Buyers will study the new figures after the 2027 revaluation, so raise a value that looks too high through the informal review. Selling sooner? Expect a buyer's agent to ask about your current bill and the combined rate for your town or fire district.

The county seat uses Newton addresses, and Hickory, Conover, Claremont, Maiden, Long View, Catawba and Brookford are the other municipalities on the tax page. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 170,172 residents, in 77,827 housing units.

Of all homes, 72.2 percent are owner-occupied, and the 2020-2024 median home value is $241,600.

faqs.q: What is the Catawba County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is .3985 per $100. Each parcel adds either a fire district rate or a town or city rate (.46 in Hickory, .45 in Newton, for instance), and the two together make the combined rate.

faqs.q: When do Catawba County property values change next?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027 is the date of the next countywide revaluation, following the one effective January 1, 2023. Catawba County revalues every four years, and appeals open once notices are mailed.

faqs.q: Which phone line handles Catawba County tax relief?
faqs.a: Call (828) 465-8436 to book a tax relief appointment, or (828) 465-8414 for general questions. Applications can be mailed to Assessor's Office, Attn: Tax Relief, Box 368, Newton, NC 28658-0368. The homestead deadline is June 1.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay off deferred circuit breaker taxes when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. A sale ends the deferment, and this year's deferred tax plus the previous three years' becomes payable with interest. Ask the tax office for the balance ahead of closing so the proceeds can cover it.

faqs.q: Is a disabled veteran exclusion available in Catawba County?
faqs.a: Yes, with no income limit. Up to $45,000 of a permanent residence's assessed value is excluded. The applicant needs discharge proof and VA certification of permanent, total service-connected disability, and June 1 is the deadline.
